quickAnswer: Upton has the lowest share of new homes of the 50 towns we serve: only 88 houses, 3.1%, were built since 2010 (ACS 2022). Meanwhile 22.4% date from 1939 or earlier and 59.7% heat with oil, so many replacements go into houses with decades behind them.
body: ## The town where almost nothing has been built lately

The Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS) counts 2,845 housing units in Upton. Only 88 of them, 3.1%, were built in 2010 or later. That is the lowest share of all 50 towns Mass HVAC serves, against 8.4% for the middle town. The median home dates to 1979, and the biggest age band is 1980 to 1999 with 854 homes (30.0%).

At the other end, 636 homes (22.4%) were built in 1939 or earlier, the 9th-highest share on our list. Another 215 (7.6%) date from 1940 to 1959 and 625 (22.0%) from 1960 to 1979. Add them up and 1,476 homes, 51.9%, predate 1980, a little below the middle town's 57.2%. A boiler or furnace going into a house of that vintage should be sized to the house, so the heating load is assessed before a system is quoted.
## Oil first, gas second, and hardly any propane

Fuel oil heats 1,631 occupied homes (59.7%, 11th-highest). Utility gas heats 740 (27.1%), against 41.9% for the middle town. Electricity heats 219 homes (8.0%), wood 76 (2.8%) and bottled or tank gas only 51 (1.9%), which ranks 46th of 50.

With 740 homes on a gas main and 1,631 on oil, the replacement question depends on which fuel the house burns now. A home on a gas main can often swap like for like. A home on oil faces a choice between a new oil system, a gas conversion if a main reaches the street, and a heat pump.
## Boots, hats and a shift from small shops to big mills

Upton was first settled in 1728 and incorporated in 1735, taking land from Hopkinton, Mendon, Uxbridge and Sutton. Between 1730 and 1850 the town had many small shoe shops called ten-footers, which were gradually merged into larger assembly-line companies, and by 1837 Upton produced 21.7% of the boots made in Worcester County. The Knowlton Hat Factory, built in 1872, was added to the National Historic Register in 1982.

Heat loss in a house of that age depends on its insulation, windows and attic more than on the number of rooms. The town covers 21.7 square miles, 21.5 of them land, and its northwestern section around Warren Brook is known locally as Forest Green for the rolling hills seen from Fowler Street and Mechanic Street.
## Multi-unit buildings and a small renter group

Detached houses make up 84.6% of Upton's units (11th-highest), but the town also has 199 homes in two-unit buildings (7.0%), 83 in buildings of three or four units (2.9%) and 108 in buildings of five or more (3.8%). Together, 390 units (13.7%) are in multi-unit buildings. Owners occupy 2,461 households (90.0%) and renters 272 (10.0%), which ranks 41st of 50. The median home value is $541,000, against $579,150 for the middle town, and vacancy is 3.9%, or 112 of the 2,845 units.
## National Grid and the new community center

Upton's electric utility is National Grid, which appears on its official Massachusetts Electric Company territory list, so Mass Save is the rebate path to check for a heat pump. The town opened the Upton Community Center on May 1, 2023, built with a $12 million bond approved at the 2021 Town Meeting; it holds a new library building, a senior center, a refurbished playground and meeting rooms. Our [heat pump page](/cities/upton/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) has the rebate terms.

faq.q: Does Upton have many new homes?
faq.a: No. Only 88 homes, 3.1% of the total, were built in 2010 or later, which is the lowest share among the 50 towns we serve. Most of the housing dates from before 2000, so a replacement boiler or furnace is often going into a house built well before it.

faq.q: Is natural gas available in Upton?
faq.a: Utility gas heats 740 Upton homes, 27.1%, and oil heats 1,631, 59.7%. Both are common, but availability depends on your street. The gas company can tell you whether a main passes your house, which decides whether a conversion from oil is possible.

faq.q: How does Upton compare with the middle town on heating fuel?
faq.a: Upton sits well above the middle town on oil, 59.7% against 36.5%, and well below it on utility gas, 27.1% against 41.9%. A replacement here therefore often turns on oil against gas against a heat pump, rather than on a single default choice.

faq.q: Will my Upton house qualify for Mass Save heat pump rebates?
faq.a: Possibly. National Grid serves Upton, so Mass Save is the path to check, and the house has to pass a weatherization test. With 51.9% of homes built before 1980, many owners may start with a Home Energy Assessment. Terms can change, so confirm at masssave.com.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Oil heats 1,631 Upton homes and utility gas 740, so a replacement here often comes down to oil, gas or a heat pump. The first question is whether a gas main runs past the house.
body: ## Two big fuels and a handful of others

Fuel oil serves 59.7% of occupied homes, 11th among the 50 towns, while utility gas serves 27.1%, 34th. Electricity heats 219 homes, wood 76, tank gas 51 and other fuels or coal 16. Against the middle town's 36.5% oil and 41.9% gas, Upton leans toward oil without being an all-oil town, so the replacement decision depends on the fuel a house burns now.
### Oil homes

A house on oil can stay with oil, convert to gas if a main reaches the street, or move to a heat pump. Staying with oil keeps the tank and chimney. A conversion needs the gas company's main, a new gas line and a venting plan.
### Gas homes and the permit

A swap of a gas boiler or furnace is often like for like. Only licensed plumbers and gas fitters can obtain a gas permit in Massachusetts, and the new furnace or boiler is normally inspected once it is in. The building department can explain its filing process.
### What the house adds to the job

The median Upton home dates to 1979, and the biggest age band, 1980 to 1999, holds 854 homes. Piping, baseboard and ducts from the original build can outlast the boiler, so a replacement has to fit what is already there, and the heating load is assessed before a system is quoted.
### Rentals

Upton has 272 renter households. A rented unit, in Upton as elsewhere in the state, has to be kept at 68 F or higher from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. and 64 F or higher overnight while the heating season runs. The landlord pays for heat unless the lease says otherwise. This is general information, not legal advice.
### At night or on a weekend
Call (508) 786-8755 for an emergency. Calls are taken 24/7, and the written estimate is free before any work starts. For the numbers on Upton's housing, see the [city page](/cities/upton).

faq.q: Can I switch from oil to gas in Upton?
faq.a: Only if a gas main runs past your property, and 740 homes in town use one. Ask the gas company first. If a main is available, price the conversion against a new oil system and a heat pump, because the cheapest start is not always the cheapest over the years.

faq.q: Is wood a main heat source for any Upton homes?
faq.a: For 76 Upton homes, 2.8%, yes. In others a stove is a supplement. Either way, the chimney and flue should be inspected before the cold season, and a stove should not be the only plan for a long outage.

faq.q: When does repairing an Upton boiler stop making sense?
faq.a: Fixing one worn part on a young boiler usually pays off. A cracked heat exchanger, repeated breakdowns or a unit far past its expected life lean toward replacing it. Ask for both options in writing so the comparison is clear.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Detached houses are 84.6% of Upton's housing, and 390 units sit in multi-unit buildings. Ducted central air fits houses with usable duct routes, and a ductless system covers the rest.
body: ## Cooling detached houses and small multi-unit buildings

Upton ranks 11th of 50 for share of single-family detached homes, with 2,407 of 2,845 units. The town also has 199 homes in two-unit buildings, 83 in buildings of three or four units, 108 in larger buildings and 48 attached townhouse units. Mobile homes number none. The type of building shapes the cooling plan, since a detached house usually has room for a condenser outside.
### Central air

A central system needs a duct network. Houses that already have forced-air heat may have one, but the ducts may be sized for heating, and cooling typically needs more airflow. Many older homes were built without central air, so new duct runs can mean opening walls and ceilings.
### Ductless

A ductless mini-split uses an outdoor unit and one or more indoor heads connected by a thin line set. It suits additions, finished attics and upstairs rooms, and it avoids duct work altogether. The same unit also heats, which is covered on the [heat pump page](/cities/upton/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
### Age of the housing

Upton's median home dates to 1979. The 515 homes built in 2000 or later, 18.1%, are the group likeliest to have ducts, while the 636 homes from 1939 or earlier are the likeliest to have none. Neither is certain, so a visit settles it. The 215 homes from 1940 through 1959 and the 625 from 1960 through 1979 fall between the two, and each one has to be looked at on its own.
### Electric homes
Electricity heats 219 Upton homes, 8.0%, the 40th-highest share of 50 towns. In those houses a heat pump can cover cooling in summer and take over part of the winter load from resistance heat.
### Size and humidity

An oversized air conditioner cools fast and then switches off before it has removed much moisture. Sizing follows the house: insulation, windows, the attic and which rooms face the afternoon sun. With 84.6% of units detached, each house is sized separately instead of by a rule of thumb, and the 21.7 square miles of the town hold a wide mix of ages.

faq.q: Can I cool just one room of my Upton house?
faq.a: Yes, a single ductless head can do that. It is a common way to cool an upstairs bedroom, an attic room or an addition. Adding heads later is possible, though the outdoor unit has limits on how many it can feed.

faq.q: Is it worth adding central air to an older Upton house?
faq.a: Sometimes. It depends on whether usable duct routes exist. If walls and ceilings would have to be opened for new ducts, a ductless system can be the simpler route. A visit shows what the house allows before any price is discussed.

faq.q: Why does my air conditioner run but not cool?
faq.a: A dirty coil, a failed capacitor, a refrigerant leak or a blocked filter are common causes. Some are small repairs and some point to an aging compressor. A technician can tell which, and the written estimate shows both options.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: Upton's electricity comes through National Grid, which points to Mass Save. With 1,631 homes on oil and 740 on utility gas, the heat pump question differs from one fuel group to the other.
body: ## A heat pump against oil or gas

Because National Grid delivers the power, Mass Save's 2026 whole-home rebate ($2,650 per ton, up to $8,500 per home) is the one to check, and the house must be weatherized first. The [general heat pump page](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) lists the other conditions, and terms can change.
### The oil group

The 1,631 oil homes are where a heat pump replaces a delivered, burned fuel, and some owners keep the boiler for the coldest days. Oil is 11th-highest in the 50 towns, so this group is large in a regional sense too, and every one of those homes has a tank to think about.
### The gas group

The 740 homes on utility gas face a different comparison, because gas is a fuel they already have. A heat pump there may be justified by its ability to cool as well as heat, or by an owner wanting less reliance on a burner. Gas holds a 27.1% share, against 41.9% for the middle town.
### Little propane

Only 51 Upton homes, 1.9%, heat with tank gas, the 46th-highest share. Propane customers are rare here, so the useful comparison is oil or gas against a heat pump, not propane against anything. The 16 homes on other fuels or coal are a small group of their own.
### Age against the weatherization test

One way to pass the weatherization test is to be built in 2000 or later. In Upton that is 515 homes, 18.1%, and only 88 date from 2010. The 1,476 homes that predate 1980 and the 854 from 1980 through 1999 sit outside that test. The 636 homes from 1939 or earlier tend to be the ones that want air sealing and insulation before a whole-home system.
### Electric homes

The 219 electric-heat homes, 8.0% of the town, form the group where a heat pump would replace resistance heat such as baseboard. A ductless system suits a house without ducts. See how it fits detached houses on the [cooling page](/cities/upton/air-conditioning-installation-repair).

faq.q: Can a heat pump handle an Upton winter by itself?
faq.a: In a tight, well-insulated house, often yes. In many others a heat pump covers most of the year and a boiler or furnace covers the coldest days. How much a heat pump can carry is decided from the home's heating load before a system is quoted.

faq.q: I have gas heat. Does a heat pump still make sense?
faq.a: It can, mostly for cooling and shoulder seasons. A heat pump heats and cools from one system. Compare the yearly cost of both fuels at your own rates, and check that your gas heat is in good condition before deciding what to retire.

faq.q: Do I need an energy assessment before installing a heat pump?
faq.a: For a whole-home rebate, a home that was not built in 2000 or later generally needs the weatherization test to be satisfied, which usually starts with a Home Energy Assessment. Confirm the current rules at masssave.com before ordering equipment.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: With 1,631 Upton homes on oil and 740 on gas, yearly service means a burner cleaning for most and a combustion check for the rest. Late summer is a good time to book before the first cold week.
body: ## Service by fuel type

Oil equipment is cleaned yearly, covering the burner, nozzle, filter and heat exchanger, with a combustion test. That covers the 59.7% of Upton homes on oil. A gas appliance gets a burner, vent and connection check. The 219 electric homes need filters and coils looked at instead, and the 76 wood homes need the chimney and flue inspected.
### What a gas visit looks like

- Burner and flame appearance
- Venting and flue condition
- Gas connections and controls
- Thermostat operation
### What an oil visit looks like

- Clean the burner and the heat exchanger
- Replace the nozzle and filter
- Test combustion and check the tank and lines
### Equipment and house age

Upton's largest age band, 1980 to 1999, holds 854 homes (30.0%), and another 625 come from 1960 through 1979. In houses of those decades, parts such as igniters, pumps and circulators may be due for attention, and the age of the unit, not the house, decides how often to look at it.

Heat pumps and cooling equipment are lighter work: clean filters, clear coils and drains, and an outdoor unit kept free of leaves and snow.
### Owners, landlords and the calendar

Owners hold 2,461 Upton households, 90.0%, and renters 272. A landlord who has the boiler serviced before the first cold week is less likely to face a no-heat complaint. For cooling equipment, spring is the natural time for a coil, drain and outdoor unit check.

### Booking and between visits
A late-summer or early-fall visit tends to be easier to schedule than one squeezed into the first cold week. Between visits, owners can glance at the tank gauge each month and look for damp spots under the tank and along the fuel line.

### Do not wait for the annual visit if

Strange sounds, a smell of oil or smoke, or a unit that starts and stops every few minutes deserve a call before the annual visit. For the air side of the house, which a burner visit does not touch, read the [air quality page](/cities/upton/indoor-air-quality).

faq.q: Does a gas furnace in Upton need a yearly tune-up?
faq.a: A yearly check is a sound habit even though gas burns cleaner than oil. The technician looks at the burner, venting and gas connections, and reports anything worn. With 740 gas homes in town, many owners are in this group.

faq.q: When is the best time to service an oil boiler?
faq.a: Late summer or early fall, before the first cold week. That timing leaves room to order a part if one is worn. A skipped year lets soot gather on the heat exchanger, which can cost efficiency.

faq.q: How should I care for a wood stove chimney?
faq.a: Have the chimney and flue inspected once a year before the first fire, and cleaned if creosote has built up. With 76 wood-heat homes in Upton, that inspection is a safety item, not an optional extra.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Upton's 2,845 homes span 636 built in 1939 or earlier and 88 built since 2010, and the air problems at the two ends are not the same.
body: ## Air in a town of older houses

The ACS 2022 puts 215 Upton homes (7.6%) in the 1940 to 1959 band, 625 (22.0%) in 1960 to 1979 and 854 (30.0%) in 1980 to 1999. Another 515 (18.1%) date from 2000 on. The 636 homes from 1939 or earlier are the oldest group, and a house can contain several eras at once, since additions often differ from the original building.
### Older houses

Older houses often have gaps around windows, sills and attic floors. That air movement can dilute some pollutants, but it can also draw in dust, pollen and damp air from the basement. The 636 homes from 1939 or earlier are where drafts and basement damp are most likely to show up. If you plan work on a very old house, ask a qualified specialist to test for lead paint or asbestos first.
### Tighter houses

Newer construction is generally tighter. The 515 homes built since 2000 may hold humidity, cooking fumes and chemicals from furnishings unless ventilation works. Bath fans and a range hood that vent outside help, and in a very tight house a mechanical ventilator can bring in fresh air. Only 88 Upton homes date from 2010, so that case is a small one.
### Dry air and damp air

Indoor air can turn dry in winter and humid in summer. A humidifier on the heating system answers the first, and a dehumidifier suits a damp basement. A thermostat reading alone does not say which problem you have, so use a hygrometer.
### Filters and ducts
Check that the blower can pull air through a denser filter before buying one. Cleaning ducts is worth considering where they are visibly dirty or moldy, or after a renovation.
### Combustion and wood

Appliances that burn oil, gas or wood need proper venting, and a carbon monoxide alarm on each floor is inexpensive protection. Wood heats 76 Upton homes; a poorly vented stove or damp wood puts smoke and fine particles indoors. See the [tune-up page](/cities/upton/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups) for the yearly check.

faq.q: Is the air in an older Upton house worse than in a newer one?
faq.a: Not by default. An older house leaks, so fresh air arrives but so do dust and damp. A tighter newer house keeps moisture and fumes in. Either can be improved once the cause is found, and the cause differs between the two.

faq.q: Do I need to clean my ducts?
faq.a: Seldom as a routine. Mold, heavy visible dirt or a renovation that disturbed the runs are the usual triggers, and plenty of houses never need it. A look at the whole system, including the filter and return, shows what would help.

faq.q: What does a whole-house humidifier do?
faq.a: It adds moisture to the air that passes through the heating system, which can ease dry skin and static in winter. It needs seasonal upkeep, and in a tight house too much humidity can condense on windows. A humidistat keeps it in range.
